subject: WellPath — training exclusion & data residency evidence
messages:
From: Diane Lopez <d.lopez@wellpathhealth.com>
To: Sean Gallagher <sean_gallagher@redwood.com>
Cc: compliance@wellpathhealth.com
Date: 2026-01-12T09:15:00-08:00
Subject: Request: training exclusion + subprocessor / residency evidence

Sean —

Thanks for taking this early look. As part of WellPath's procurement and privacy review we need to confirm a few items before we proceed to final approval:

- Contractual "no-training" commitment for any patient-identifiable or clinical-text content ingested into Redwood's inference endpoints (i.e., you will not use our customer data to update model weights or for model improvement).
- A current list of subprocessors (hosting, logs, telemetry) with locations and contract start dates.
- Artifacts showing how you can provide evidence (audit logs, exportable ingest samples, or signed statements) that no training occurs on our data.
- Data residency options: priority for US-only (us-east-1) storage and processing; if any EU or APAC subprocessors are involved, please flag them.

I've attached our short questionnaire for vendors (WellPath_DPA_Questionnaire.pdf). Our legal counsel (Oliver) will be copied on later exchanges if needed.

We are aiming to finalize vendor terms by Jan 29; can you confirm a path to provide the artifacts and a one-page signed confirmation of the no-train commitment?

Thanks,
Diane Lopez
Head of Digital Privacy — WellPath Health
[d.lopez@wellpathhealth.com]

[Attachment: WellPath_DPA_Questionnaire.pdf]

From: Sean Gallagher <sean_gallagher@redwood.com>
To: Diane Lopez <d.lopez@wellpathhealth.com>
Cc: Kimberly Park <kimberly_park@redwood.com>, Laura Bennett <laura_bennett@redwood.com>
Date: 2026-01-12T11:08:00-08:00
Subject: Re: Request: training exclusion + subprocessor / residency evidence

Diane —

Appreciate the clear ask and the timeline. Short answers up front: we can (1) contractually agree to a scoped "no-training" commitment for customer data, (2) provide a current subprocessor manifest and (3) assemble an evidence pack that includes sampled ingest logs and an audit statement. What we need to confirm with you:

- Scope: does "no-training" need to include aggregated telemetry/usage metrics, or only raw prompt/response data and attachments?
- Residency: is US-only processing a strict requirement for all environments, or only for production customer data?
- Evidence format: will a signed one-page statement + a zipped evidence bundle (audit logs, subprocessor list, SOC pointer) satisfy your procurement team?

Next steps from our side: I've looped in Kimberly (legal) and Laura (security/compliance) to assemble a redline and an evidence bundle. We'll prepare a draft redline (redline_dpa_v3.pdf), the subprocessor CSV, and a no_train_evidence.zip containing sampled ingress logs.

Can you confirm whether Oliver should be included on the next exchange, and whether there's any specific format the procurement team requires for the signed confirmation?

Best,
Sean Gallagher
Director, Enterprise Sales — Redwood Inference
sean_gallagher@redwood.com | +1-415-555-0123

From: Laura Bennett <laura_bennett@redwood.com>
To: Sean Gallagher <sean_gallagher@redwood.com>
Cc: Marcus Lin <marcus_lin@redwood.com>, Kimberly Park <kimberly_park@redwood.com>
Date: 2026-01-13T08:42:00-08:00
Subject: Fwd: Request: training exclusion + subprocessor / residency evidence

Sean —

Notes on artifacts to prepare (security + compliance POV):

- Subprocessor manifest: CSV with service role, vendor name, primary region, contract start date, and data access scope (we should mark anything with ability to access content). File: subprocessor_list_20260115.csv
- Evidence pack (no_train_evidence.zip):
  - signed_no_train_statement.txt (one-page signed declaration from Redwood legal + timestamp)
  - ingest-logs-sample.csv (sample, redacted PII, preserved hashes/timestamps)
  - audit-config.yaml (shows logging retention and export endpoints)
  - model-serving-config.yaml (shows telemetry toggles; we can demonstrate telemetry-disabled profile)
- Controls we can offer: telemetry toggle per-customer, KMS-backed key for customer blobs, exportable audit pack with sha256 hashes.

Legal redlines I recommend:
- Insert explicit language: "Provider will not use Customer Data to train, fine-tune, or improve models except with Customer's prior written consent."
- Define operational telemetry carve-out: "Provider may collect non-content telemetry necessary for service health, monitoring, and billing; such telemetry will be aggregated and cannot be back-projected to recreate Customer inputs/outputs."
- Ownership: "Customer retains ownership of Inputs and Outputs; Provider retains aggregated operational logs for up to X days only for diagnostics."

Marcus — can you validate that the evidence pack contents are producible in the next 48 hours and that the ingest-logs-sample is safe to hand off after redaction?

Laura
Director, Security & Compliance — Redwood Inference

From: Marcus Lin <marcus_lin@redwood.com>
To: Laura Bennett <laura_bennett@redwood.com>, Sean Gallagher <sean_gallagher@redwood.com>
Cc: Kimberly Park <kimberly_park@redwood.com>
Date: 2026-01-13T10:17:00-08:00
Subject: Re: Fwd: Request: training exclusion + subprocessor / residency evidence

Laura / Sean —

We can produce the evidence pack and the redacted ingest sample. Execution notes:

- Telemetry: toggle already exists in the serving config (see model-serving-config.yaml); when enabled per-customer, we stop capturing KV cache dumps and disable opt-in telemetry routing.
- Ingest logs: we will generate a 500-row sampled CSV (ingest-logs-sample.csv) where PII is replaced by stable hashed identifiers; timestamps and request hashes remain so the customer can verify ingestion but not reconstruct content.
- Signed statement: legal can sign a short confirmation; operations can provide signed artifact with a timestamp from our internal KMS key (proof of issuance).
- Subprocessors: CSV will include cloud provider region, logging vendor, and a note on whether the subprocessor handles content or metadata. We have one EU logging vendor in staging only — will mark as not used in production.

I'll assemble no_train_evidence.zip and the subprocessor CSV by EOD tomorrow.

—Marcus
Senior Product Engineer — Redwood Inference

From: Sean Gallagher <sean_gallagher@redwood.com>
To: Diane Lopez <d.lopez@wellpathhealth.com>
Cc: Kimberly Park <kimberly_park@redwood.com>, Laura Bennett <laura_bennett@redwood.com>, Oliver Klein <oliver.klein@wellpathlegal.com>
Date: 2026-01-15T16:22:00-08:00
Subject: Re: Request: training exclusion + subprocessor / residency evidence

Diane —

Thanks — attaching the items we discussed. High level: Redwood will agree to a scoped no-training commitment (we'll provide a one-page signed statement) for all customer Inputs and Outputs; operational telemetry will remain for service health but will be aggregated and cannot be used to train models.

Attachments delivered:
- redline_dpa_v3.pdf (legal redline with proposed clause: "no use of Customer Data to train or improve models without prior written consent")
- subprocessor_list_20260115.csv (current manifest; flagged staging EU logging vendor as non-production)
- no_train_evidence.zip (signed_no_train_statement.txt, ingest-logs-sample.csv, model-serving-config.yaml, audit-config.yaml)
- ingest-logs-sample.csv (separate quick view)

Additional links: SOC2 report: https://drive.redwood.com/reports/Redwood_SOC2_2025.pdf
Evidence folder (zipped): https://drive.redwood.com/shared/WellPath/no-train-evidence

Proposed next steps:
1) Legal review of redline_dpa_v3.pdf — please provide comments by Jan 22 if possible.
2) Confirm residency requirement: if WellPath requires hard US-only processing in production, we'll add migration/region-locking notes in the DPA.
3) If a signed confirmation is sufficient, let us know who from WellPath will sign and we'll return our one-page signed statement.

If it helps, I'm available for a 20‑minute call on Jan 19 to walk Oliver and your procurement team through the artifacts.

Best regards,
Sean Gallagher
Director, Enterprise Sales — Redwood Inference
[Attachment: redline_dpa_v3.pdf, subprocessor_list_20260115.csv, no_train_evidence.zip, ingest-logs-sample.csv]

From: Diane Lopez <d.lopez@wellpathhealth.com>
To: Sean Gallagher <sean_gallagher@redwood.com>
Cc: Oliver Klein <oliver.klein@wellpathlegal.com>, compliance@wellpathhealth.com
Date: 2026-01-15T17:05:00-08:00
Subject: Re: Request: training exclusion + subprocessor / residency evidence

Sean —

Received, thank you. This looks promising. Two quick asks: (1) please send the one-page signed confirmation as a separate PDF with a corporate signature block so our procurement legal team can attach it to the vendor file, and (2) for the ingest sample, can you include a line that maps the sample row hash to the original ingest timestamp (we need to confirm ingestion happened within our anticipated window).

Oliver — can you confirm if we need any additional language beyond the redline Sean shared?

We'll schedule a 20-minute call for Jan 19; I'll send an invite shortly.

Best,
Diane
Head of Digital Privacy — WellPath Health
[Attachment: none]
